{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Re-express the analysis to account for confounding by customer_segment
# We will compute the treatment effect within each segment, then combine them

# Compute conversion rate and average revenue for each channel within each segment
# This is the correct way to assess campaign effect: compare within segments

# Conversion rate by channel and segment
conv_by_seg = data_clean.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['converted'].mean().reset_index()
conv_by_seg = conv_by_seg.pivot(index='channel', columns='customer_segment', values='converted')

# Revenue by channel and segment
rev_by_seg = data_clean.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['revenue_clean'].mean().reset_index()
rev_by_seg = rev_by_seg.pivot(index='channel', columns='customer_segment', values='revenue_clean')

# Compute within-segment differences
conv_diff = conv_by_seg.loc['email'] - conv_by_seg.loc['paid_search']
rev_diff = rev_by_seg.loc['email'] - rev_by_seg.loc['paid_search']

# Summary
print("Within-segment differences in conversion rate:")
print(conv_diff)

print("\nWithin-segment differences in average revenue:")
print(rev_diff)

# Overall summary
print("\nSummary of campaign effect by segment:")
for seg in ['loyal', 'new', 'returning']:
    email_conv = conv_by_seg.loc['email', seg]
    paid_conv = conv_by_seg.loc['paid_search', seg]
    email_rev = rev_by_seg.loc['email', seg]
    paid_rev = rev_by_seg.loc['paid_search', seg]
    print(f"{seg.capitalize()}: email conversion {email_conv:.3f} vs paid_search {paid_conv:.3f}; email revenue {email_rev:.2f} vs paid_search {paid_rev:.2f}")"}
